title: Stakeholder Incident Briefing and Commitment Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the standard process, timelines, and templated communications used by Customer Success and Support when briefing external stakeholders during enterprise-impacting incidents. It focuses on transparency, measurable commitments, and handoffs between Support, SRE, Product, and the customer during the first 72 hours of an outage or degradation that affects customer SLAs or business-critical flows (API availability, sustained high latency, model-quality regressions).

Goals
------
- Provide a repeatable, low-friction briefing and commitment cadence for enterprise customers.
- Set clear, measurable commitments for status updates, mitigations, and remediation windows.
- Ensure coordinated internal ownership and minimize customer uncertainty.
- Record the timeline and decisions for post-incident reviews and QBRs.

When to use this playbook
------------------------
Use for incidents that meet any of the following: 
1) Customer-facing API availability < 99.0% for > 30 minutes for an enterprise tenant.
2) Median 95th-percentile latency breach above committed SLO for > 45 minutes.
3) Model degradation/regression causing a measurable drop in eval-set quality (>10% regression on customer-critical prompts or metric) that impacts user experience.
4) Data exposure or sensitive data handling incidents (coordinate with Security).

Severity mapping and quick reference
----------------------------------
- Sev 1 (Critical): Customer production traffic impacted, no viable fallback, sustained >30 minutes. Immediate executive notification and daily remediation commitments.
- Sev 2 (High): Significant degradation affecting key flows (>45 minutes) with partial fallbacks possible. Frequent updates and defined remediation windows.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Intermittent errors, minor latency spikes, or localized features affected. Routine operational updates.

Escalation timeline and customer commitments (first 72 hours)
-----------------------------------------------------------
1) Initial Acknowledgement (T+15 minutes)
   - Action: Support triages, assigns internal incident owner.
   - Commitment to customer: Acknowledge receipt, provide preliminary impact statement, state that a follow-up will arrive within 30 minutes.
   - Owner: Support Engineer (primary) + Customer Success Manager (CSM) notified.

2) First Briefing (T+45 minutes)
   - Action: Internal tech summary from SRE/runtime team, known scope, and immediate mitigations.
   - Commitment to customer: 30–45 minute update with severity classification and initial ETA or mitigation plan (if available).
   - Owner: Incident Lead (from SRE/infra) + Support lead.

3) Hourly Operational Updates (T+1–T+6 hours)
   - Action: Hourly status messages documenting progress, blockers, and next steps.
   - Commitment to customer: Hourly notes via agreed channel until mitigation in place. If progress is faster/slower, communicate revised cadence.
   - Owner: Incident Lead + CSM for customer-facing phrasing.

4) Stabilization Notice (when service within SLO for two consecutive intervals or rollback applied)
   - Action: Declare stabilization, describe steps taken, and next actions to full remediation.
   - Commitment to customer: Stabilization message with remediation ETA for full resolution (if partial mitigation applied).
   - Owner: Incident Lead + Product/Runtime owner.

5) Final Resolution and Follow-up (within 72 hours where possible)
   - Action: Publish root-cause hypothesis, workaround/mitigation timeline, permanent fix ETA, and customer compensation if SLA breached.
   - Commitment to customer: Post-incident report (PIR) within 72 hours (initial PIR) and final PIR within 7–14 business days depending on complexity.
   - Owner: Incident Lead + CSM + designated author (Product or SRE).

Roles & responsibilities (RACI-style)
-------------------------------------
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): Account communications, stakeholder coordination, and expectations management (Responsible).
- Support Engineer: Triage, reproducer, telemetry collection, and first-line mitigation (Responsible).
- Incident Lead (SRE/Product): Technical decisions, cross-team coordination, declare stabilization and resolution (Accountable).
- Runtime/Product Owner: Implement permanent fixes and post-incident remediations (Responsible).
- Security Representative: Lead for any PII/exposure or security-sensitive escalation (Consulted).
- Legal/Privacy: Consulted if breach reaches regulatory thresholds (Consulted).
- Executive Sponsor (if escalated): Communicates high-level commitments to customer executives (Informed/Accountable as needed).

Communication channels and customer preferences
---------------------------------------------
- Primary channels: Dedicated Slack channel (customer-specific private channel), secure email thread, and the customer's status page integration.
- For customers requiring SSO/VPN: use the approved secure channel documented on the account.
- For enterprise customers with ServiceNow/JIRA integration: file incident tickets with linked updates.

Customer message templates (do not copy verbatim; personalize per account)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
1) Initial Acknowledgement (T+15)
Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident Acknowledgement for [CUSTOMER] (INC#[ID])
Body: Hello [NAME],
We received reports of an issue affecting [brief scope]. Our Support team has opened an incident (ID: INC#[ID]). We are triaging and will provide the first technical update within 45 minutes. Current impact: [high/medium/low].
Contacts: Your CSM [CSM NAME] (cc'd) and our Incident Lead [NAME].

2) First Briefing (T+45)
Subject: Redwood Inference — Initial Incident Update for [CUSTOMER] (INC#[ID])
Body: Hello [NAME],
Summary: [High-level summary of impact].
What we know: [bullet short facts].
What we are doing: [immediate actions].
Next update: [time or cadence].
ETA/mitigation estimate: [if available].

3) Hourly Update
Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident Update (INC#[ID]) — [HH:MM UTC]
Body: Hello [NAME],
Progress: [what changed since last update].
Blockers: [current blocker].
Next actions: [short next steps].
Estimated time to resolved (if changed): [ETA].

4) Stabilization Notice
Subject: Redwood Inference — Service Stabilized for [CUSTOMER] (INC#[ID])
Body: Hello [NAME],
We have applied [mitigation/rollback] and observed service returning to expected levels for [observation period]. Next steps: permanent fix ETA [X days]. We will provide the PIR within 72 hours.

5) Post-Incident Report (PIR) initial (within 72 hours)
Include: timeline, root-cause hypothesis, actions taken, mitigation applied, customer impact summary (tokens impacted, requests failed, percent SLA breach), and next steps for permanent remediation.

Metrics to capture and include in communications
-----------------------------------------------
- API availability percentage by tenant during window (per 15m interval).
- 95th/99th latency percentiles for affected endpoints.
- Token counts and cost delta for retried requests or fallback models.
- Number of affected users/requests and percentage of normal traffic.
- Any billing/SLA credit calculations (pass-through to finance).

Ownership and internal runbook checklist (for the incident lead)
--------------------------------------------------------------
1) Validate customer identity and scope (account ID, region, tenant).
2) Collect core telemetry: model IDs, versions, instance fleet, recent deployments, kernel/quantization changes.
3) Ensure reproducibility or capture request traces (sampling 1:1000 by default for initial investigation).
4) Engage SRE/runtime, product, and security as applicable.
5) Establish customer communication cadence and channel.
6) Document every update in the incident channel and link to the PIR doc.

Examples of mitigations and authorized actions (typical for Redwood)
------------------------------------------------------------------
- Fallback to compatible model variant (e.g., lower-latency quantized variant) for affected routes.
- Temporarily throttle non-critical batch jobs or background telemetry to free capacity.
- Rollback recent runtime kernel or rollout that correlated with regression.
- Apply temporary routing to an alternate region or Dedicated pool if available.
- Toggle prefix/KV cache invalidation if cache inconsistency suspected.

Compensation and SLA handling guidance
-------------------------------------
- If availability < promised SLA for invoice period, calculate credits per contract terms and notify Finance.
- For short outages where incident is declared and confirmed, include the incident reference in the credit calculation and follow the standard refund/credit workflow.
- CSM should escalate to Sales/Account Executive for discussions beyond standard credit terms.

Post-incident: handoff to QBR and remediation tracking
-----------------------------------------------------
- The PIR author and Incident Lead ensure the remediation action items are tracked in a shared ticket (JIRA / Confluence action tracker).
- CSM schedules a remediation review within 2 weeks to present status during the next QBR or a dedicated remediation meeting.
- Track remediation progress as a QBR agenda item until closed. Include a short customer-facing slide pack summarizing impact, fixes, and steps taken to prevent recurrence.

Privacy and legal considerations
------------------------------
- If PII or regulated data is involved, pause customer messaging until Security and Legal provide the approved template.
- All logs shared externally must be redacted per the customer contract and data residency rules.

Templates & attachments (internal links)
--------------------------------------
- Incident communications calendar (link): /confluence/templates/incident-calendar
- PIR template (link): /confluence/templates/pir-template
- SLA credit calculation worksheet (link): /confluence/finance/sla-credit-worksheet

Appendix: Quick example incident timeline (fictional)
--------------------------------------------------
- 10:02 UTC: Customer reports elevated 5xx for /v1/generate. Support opens INC#2026-334.
- 10:10 UTC: Initial triage shows node oom in region us-west2; incident declared Sev 1.
- 10:40 UTC: First briefing — mitigation: throttle batch jobs, spin up dedicated burst pool.
- 11:30 UTC: Partial stabilization after scaling; hourly updates continue.
- 13:15 UTC: Rollback of recent runtime patch correlated with issue; service returns to SLO.
- 15:00 UTC: Stabilization notice sent. Initial PIR drafted and shared within 48 hours.

End of playbook.
